fault.rule: non-corner core with the largest computation busy time (tensor + vector unit) in the pre-fault final evaluation; ties -> smallest (die, core)

notes: R0: pre-fault mapping, sources, routes, comm ids and event order injected on the faulty platform; communications whose route uses a failed link/node are re-routed by the artifact's Dijkstra (against the link loads of the kept routes); no SA (random/np.random seeded 123 where SA would start, as anneal() does). W(steps, t_max): same start, then the original StreamOptimization with that budget; t_min and loss ratios as in the task. Migration vs the pre-fault mapping: behaviours whose computation location changed; weight reads whose DDR source changed (primary; matched by bytes and consumer) and data_dict-based weight bytes (secondary; data_dict is stale after SA). Node faults: R0 moves each behaviour of the failed core to the nearest healthy device of its type (Manhattan on the global core grid), least loaded first, then smallest id. FULL: each of the 14 variants (greedy0/1 x lossratio0-6) run unchanged on the faulty platform (template steps and t_max); best = smallest 3-seed mean. Wall times: sa_wall = stream_mapping only; eval_wall = one backend evaluation; processes ran in parallel, so walls include contention.
